rationale: All three lenses ran. Acceptance audited the change against all 8 part-1 criteria and returned pass on every one, verifying each in source and tests rather than from the plan; it also corrected the ticket's count — there are 6 real initialize() call sites, the 7th was a docstring example at single_usage.py:68. Blind and edge-case independently converged on four actionable defects, two of them experimentally verified against the pinned mcp 1.28.1. The strongest is that the run's own recorded decision to do no sanitizing here is wrong at the trust boundary: this service, not the consumer, is what turns an arbitrary third-party server's bytes into a field the platform feeds to an LLM, and it caches that string for the whole session TTL. 4 findings emitted (all triage: patch). 1 finding deferred (cached instructions go stale for the cache TTL with no re-handshake path — worth a README note, not a blocker). 3 findings dismissed: the method-name .strip() guard (unreachable input, harmless), the missing debug log on the unknown-result fall-through (subsumed by CR-003's logging), and the blind lens's call for an env toggle to sequence rollout (it could not see that the sole consumer, the codemie backend's MCPListToolsResponse, ignores unknown fields, so no strict client breaks).

findings.title: Third-party instruction text is relayed with no length cap or control-character stripping
findings.problem: attach_server_instructions checks only isinstance(str) and .strip() truthiness. Whatever the remote server returned at handshake is copied verbatim into the tools/list response — no maximum length, no control-character or ANSI stripping, no log of its size. On the pooled path the string is captured once and re-emitted on every tools/list for the whole cache TTL.
findings.impact: A hostile or compromised MCP server registered by any tenant can inject arbitrary prompt text into every downstream LLM system prompt that consumes the field, and can return a multi-megabyte string that this service caches and re-serialises on every tools/list page, inflating response size and downstream token cost with nothing in the logs to explain it.
findings.recommendation: Cap and normalize in attach_server_instructions before attaching: truncate to a configurable maximum (e.g. MCP_CONNECT_MAX_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS, default a few KB, following the existing bare-os.getenv config pattern) and strip control characters, logging a warning with the original length when truncation fires. Escaping for prompt context stays with the consuming backend; a size ceiling and control-character strip at the trust boundary is not 'silently altering the payload'.

findings.title: A server's own top-level `instructions` key on the tools/list result is silently overwritten
findings.problem: mcp.types.Result is extra="allow", so the SDK preserves extra top-level keys a server puts on its tools/list result. Both helper branches assign unconditionally, replacing a server-supplied `instructions` with the handshake value. Verified on the pinned 1.28.1: ListToolsResult.model_validate({'tools': [], 'instructions': 'from-server', 'foo': 1}) comes back with instructions='from-handshake', foo untouched.
findings.impact: Data loss on the response contract, and a consumer cannot tell whether the value came from the handshake or from the list result. The bridge is a transparent proxy everywhere else; this is the one place it rewrites server-authored content, and the README describes the field as purely additive.
findings.recommendation: Do not overwrite an existing key: skip (logging a warning) when the result already carries a non-null `instructions`. If overwriting is ever intended, say so explicitly in the README instead of leaving it implied.

findings.title: Unguarded setattr on the SDK result can turn a successful tools/list into an HTTP 500
findings.problem: hasattr(result, "model_dump") is used as a proxy for 'pydantic model I may add a field to'. That holds only while the model is extra="allow" and not frozen; on a frozen or extra="forbid" model pydantic v2 raises ValueError. Both call sites sit inside a broad `except Exception` that maps anything to HTTP 500 (routes.py:224-238; single_usage.py:169-195/234-260/307-333). The docstring also claims dict results are copied while pydantic results are mutated in place, so the two branches have different aliasing semantics than documented.
findings.impact: Latent today because 1.28.1 is extra="allow". After an SDK bump that tightens Result config, every tools/list on every transport returns 500 — the listing succeeded but the response is destroyed, and the cause is far from the symptom. The in-place mutation also stamps a result object the SDK may retain or share between concurrent requests on one pooled client.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the assignment in try/except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError), log a warning and return the untouched result; or use result.model_copy(update={"instructions": ...}) so both branches copy. Reconcile the docstring with whichever is chosen, and add a unit test passing a model with extra="forbid" that asserts the result comes back unchanged.

findings.title: Tests cover 2 of 6 transport bodies, never the production pydantic path, and the only real-SDK assertion is deselected by default
findings.problem: Six initialize bodies changed (managed and single-usage x stdio/streamable-http/sse); the new tests exercise streamable-http only on each path. Every mocked /bridge test stubs list_tools to return a plain dict, taking the isinstance(dict) branch — a branch that never runs in production, where the SDK returns ListToolsResult. The one test using real SDK types is marked integration and pyproject sets addopts = "-m 'not integration'", so the default run deselects it; this repo has no CI to run it separately.
findings.impact: A future refactor reverting one of the four uncovered bodies to ready_future.set_result(session) — the exact 30-second-hang failure mode the technical analysis warned about — stays green. So does any regression in the route-level pydantic serialization that the whole backward-compatibility argument rests on.
findings.recommendation: Parametrize the managed and single-usage instruction tests over all three transports; change at least one /bridge test so the mocked session returns a real mcp.types.ListToolsResult; and either run the integration marker as a documented gate in quality-gates.md or move an equivalent real-types assertion into the default suite.
